The first path indicates that Bremelanotide targets the IgG receptor FcRn large subunit p51, which is subsequently targeted by a compound with the structure (2S)-2-Amino-4-((carboxycarbonyl)amino)butanoic acid. This compound, in turn, has a target of RWLeu4. The second path reveals that Bremelanotide also targets Calu-1, which is targeted by a more complex compound that ultimately also targets RWLeu4. While the evidence is consistent across both paths, the strength of the relationship between Bremelanotide and RWLeu4 is moderate, as indicated by the final scores of 0.5457 and 0.4989, respectively. The mechanisms involve the interaction of Bremelanotide with different molecular targets, suggesting a potential role in modulating the activity of RWLeu4 through multiple pathways. The evidence supports a possible involvement of Bremelanotide in regulating RWLeu4, but further research is needed to clarify the exact nature of this interaction.
